text:
emily-sec: Security advisory: detection of plaintext Kafka credentials in application logs forwarded to our central logging cluster. This impacts the topic cluster-prod-us and could allow an attacker with log access to produce/consume. Immediate actions below.

kai-logging: How did creds get into logs? is this from an app or an agent?

emily-sec: Root cause: a change in a backend service (services/metric-ingester) added debug logging that interpolated full connection strings. Example log line from ELK:
```2026-03-22T18:12:03Z INFO connector:init connecting to kafka://user:PASTE_ME@kafka-cluster.prod.internal:9093/ - starting consumer```

sec-bot: Automated detector flagged 45 log lines in last 72h containing regex (kafka|bootstrap) with patterns matching credential-like tokens. Incident id: sec-2026-045.

tara-backend: Ack. That is from a temporary troubleshooting change I landed last week (I thought the token was redacted). I'll revert the change.

dom-platform: We need containment first. Oncall-infra: can you rotate the service user credentials for cluster-prod-us and depress any long-lived creds?

oncall-infra: Starting rotation now. Will create a new service principal and replace keystore entries. ETA ~30m for rotation and CI rollout.

emily-sec: Action items for teams: 1) Immediately identify any services that logged Kafka connection strings in the last 7 days. Run: ```curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/search?q=connector:init+connecting+to+kafka" | jq '.hits.hits[]._source.path' | sort -u``` 2) Remove any hardcoded connection strings; use KMS-backed secrets or workload identity. 3) Reindex logs to redact sensitive fields (see step 4).

kai-logging: We'll apply a filter to redact host:port:user:pass patterns in the logging ingestion pipeline and create a retrospective scrub job for the last 30 days. Pipeline rule: replace /([\w\-]+):([\w\-]+)@([\w\-\.]+:\d+)/ with [REDACTED_KAFKA_CONN].

emily-sec: Also: rotate any Kafka ACL tokens and audit ACLs for broad consumer groups. If your service used the exposed creds, assume compromise and rotate: service account keys, JAAS configs, and any stored keystores. High-risk services (ingesters, CI pipelines, alerting) must rotate within 2 hours. Others within 24 hours.

tara-backend: Confirmed revert pushed to main. Opening PR to strip logs and add a logging test to prevent future leakage. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/metric-ingester/pulls/128

dom-platform: We'll push an automated check in CI: fail build if any commit introduces patterns matching secret-like Kafka URIs. I'll add a pre-merge hook and update the linter.

emily-sec: Forensics: if you used a shared laptop or a VM where these services were run interactively, mark the host for a scan. Provide hostnames into the incident tracker. Do not share any secrets in Slack.

kai-logging: Scrub job started for last 30 days (job id LK-7789). We'll replace matched fields with a deterministic hash and store a mapping securely for rotation verification.

oncall-infra: Rotation completed for cluster-prod-us service accounts. New creds pushed via secrets manager and deployments are rolling. Monitoring consumer lags and unauthorized produce attempts.

sec-bot: Incident sec-2026-045 update: creds rotation completed (2115604555). Redaction pipeline applied (2115604622). 3 services flagged as high-risk and quarantined for token replacement.

tara-backend: Tests added and log line assertion in place. I also put a note in CONTRIBUTING.md about never logging URIs or raw auth.

emily-sec: Post-action checklist: 1) confirm redeploy with new secrets 2) verify no unknown consumer groups in the cluster 3) complete retrospective on why debug log reached prod. We'll publish a short advisory to the company: rotate any stored Kafka connection strings and audit access to logging dashboards.

dom-platform: I'll follow up with a permanent logging policy: redact by default for connectors and any URI containing credentials.

emily-sec: Thank you. If you find anything unusual in your service after rotation, ping #eng-security and tag @emily-sec. We'll produce a post-incident summary after root cause and retrospective (target EOD).
